yaml.title: 8. Differential equations
yaml.subtitle: Separation of variables · initial conditions · mathematical models

markdown.markdown:
::: {.callout-important} 本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 3.8：把简单 rate-of-change statement 写成 differential equation；用 separation of variables 和 integration 解一阶 differential equation；使用 initial condition 求 particular solution；解释解在 model 中的含义。 本章的 P3 note 文件夹没有独立的 Differential equations 笔记 PDF，因此这里不添加未经来源支持的 note 图片；知识点用公式卡呈现，真题题干直接按 past paper 保留。 ::: ## 1. Core knowledge ::: {.formula-panel} ### Separation of variables 若 $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=F(x)G(y), $$ 先把 $y$ 的因子与 $dy$ 放在一边，把 $x$ 的因子与 $dx$ 放在另一边，再分别积分： $$ \frac{dy}{G(y)}=F(x)\,dx. $$ 积分常数必须在使用 initial condition 后确定。若最后需要 $y$，还要根据 initial condition 选择正确的 branch。 ::: ::: {.worked-example} Knowledge-point example · particular solution 若 $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=x e^{y-x},\qquad y=0\text{ when }x=0, $$ 则 $$ e^{-y}\,dy=xe^{-x}\,dx \Longrightarrow -e^{-y}=-(x+1)e^{-x}+C. $$ 代入 $(x,y)=(0,0)$ 得 $C=0$，所以 $$ \boxed{y=x-\ln(x+1)}. $$ ::: ::: {.formula-panel} ### Model interpretation 比例关系必须先写出比例常数，例如 $$ \frac{dx}{dt}\propto x(300-x) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{dx}{dt}=k x(300-x). $$ 再用一个已知的 rate value 求 $k$。最后的 particular solution 要满足 initial condition，并且应在题目给出的物理范围内取值。 ::: ## 2. Paper 3 past-paper questions 以下 20 题的英文题干按原始 past paper 保留；只把 PDF 中的排版符号规范为 LaTeX。答案按对应 mark scheme 的积分与 initial-condition 得分点展开。 ### Separable equations in $x$ and $y$ ::: {.question-card #de-q01} ### Question 1 · 9709/32/M/J/20 Q7 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y-1}{(x+1)(x+3)}. $$ It is given that $y=2$ when $x=0$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[9]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{y-1}=\frac{dx}{(x+1)(x+3)} =\frac12\left(\frac1{x+1}-\frac1{x+3}\right)dx. $$ 因此 $$ \ln|y-1|=\frac12\ln\left|\frac{x+1}{x+3}\right|+C. $$ 由 $y=2$ when $x=0$，并且 $y-1>0$： $$ y-1=\sqrt{\frac{3(x+1)}{x+3}}, \qquad \boxed{y=1+\sqrt{\frac{3(x+1)}{x+3}}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-32.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q02} ### Question 2 · 9709/32/O/N/20 Q7 The variables $x$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ e^{3t}\frac{dx}{dt}=\cos^2 2x, $$ for $t\ge0$. It is given that $x=0$ when $t=0$. (a) Solve the differential equation and obtain an expression for $x$ in terms of $t$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \sec^2(2x)\,dx=e^{-3t}\,dt. $$ 积分得 $$ \frac12\tan(2x)=-\frac13e^{-3t}+C. $$ 代入 $x=0$ when $t=0$ 得 $C=1/3$，所以 $$ \tan(2x)=\frac23(1-e^{-3t}). $$ 由于 $x=0$ 时取 principal branch， $$ \boxed{x=\frac12\tan^{-1}\left(\frac23(1-e^{-3t})\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_32.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q03} ### Question 3 · 9709/32/F/M/21 Q4 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ (1-\cos x)\frac{dy}{dx}=y\sin x. $$ It is given that $y=4$ when $x=\pi$. (a) Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[6]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac1y\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\sin x}{1-\cos x} =\frac{d}{dx}\ln(1-\cos x). $$ 因此 $y=C(1-\cos x)$。由 $y=4$ when $x=\pi$： $$ 4=C(1-(-1))=2C\Longrightarrow C=2. $$ 故 $$ \boxed{y=2(1-\cos x)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_32.pdf`, Q4, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q04} ### Question 4 · 9709/31/M/J/21 Q10 The variables $x$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dx}{dt}=x^2(1+2x), $$ and $x=1$ when $t=0$. Using partial fractions, solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $t$ in terms of $x$. **[11]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dt}{dx}=\frac1{x^2(1+2x)} =-\frac2x+\frac1{x^2}+\frac4{1+2x}. $$ 积分并使用 $t=0$ when $x=1$： $$ t=-2\ln x-\frac1x+2\ln(1+2x)+1-2\ln3. $$ 整理为 $$ \boxed{t=2\ln\left(\frac{1+2x}{3x}\right)+1-\frac1x}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_31.pdf`, Q10, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q05} ### Question 5 · 9709/32/O/N/21 Q7 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ e^{2x}\frac{dy}{dx}=4xy^2, $$ and it is given that $y=1$ when $x=0$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ y^{-2}\,dy=4xe^{-2x}\,dx. $$ Since $$ \int4xe^{-2x}dx=-(2x+1)e^{-2x}, $$ we have $$ -\frac1y=-(2x+1)e^{-2x}+C. $$ At $(x,y)=(0,1)$, $C=0$. Hence $$ \boxed{y=\frac{e^{2x}}{2x+1}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_32.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q06} ### Question 6 · 9709/32/F/M/22 Q9 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ (x+1)(3x+1)\frac{dy}{dx}=y, $$ and it is given that $y=1$ when $x=1$. Solve the differential equation and find the exact value of $y$ when $x=3$, giving your answer in a simplified form. **[9]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{y}=\frac{dx}{(x+1)(3x+1)},qquad \frac1{(x+1)(3x+1)}=-\frac1{2(x+1)}+\frac3{2(3x+1)}. $$ Thus $$ \ln y=\frac12\ln\left(\frac{3x+1}{x+1}\right)+C. $$ Using $y=1$ at $x=1$ gives $C=\frac12\ln2$, so $$ y=\sqrt{\frac{2(3x+1)}{x+1}}. $$ At $x=3$, $$ \boxed{y=\sqrt5}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_32.pdf`, Q9, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q07} ### Question 7 · 9709/31/M/J/22 Q4 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{xy}{1+x^2}, $$ and $y=2$ when $x=0$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining a simplified expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{y}=\frac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx \Longrightarrow \ln y=\frac12\ln(1+x^2)+C. $$ At $x=0,y=2$, $C=\ln2$. Hence $$ \boxed{y=2\sqrt{1+x^2}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_31.pdf`, Q4, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q08} ### Question 8 · 9709/32/M/J/22 Q6 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=xe^{y-x}, $$ and $y=0$ when $x=0$. (a) Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ e^{-y}\,dy=xe^{-x}\,dx. $$ Integrating, $$ -e^{-y}=-(x+1)e^{-x}+C. $$ The initial condition gives $C=0$, so $$ e^{-y}=(x+1)e^{-x} \Longrightarrow \boxed{y=x-\ln(x+1)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_32.pdf`, Q6, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q09} ### Question 9 · 9709/32/O/N/22 Q7(a–b) The variables $x$ and $\theta$ satisfy the differential equation $$ x\sin^2\theta\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\tan^2\theta-2\cot\theta, $$ for $0<\theta<\frac12\pi$ and $x>0$. It is given that $x=2$ when $\theta=\frac14\pi$. (a) Show that $$ \frac{d}{d\theta}(\cot^2\theta)=-\frac{2\cot\theta}{\sin^2\theta}. $$ (You may assume without proof that the derivative of $\cot\theta$ with respect to $\theta$ is $-\cosec^2\theta$.) (b) Solve the differential equation and find the value of $x$ when $\theta=\frac16\pi$. **[1+7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer (a) $$ \frac{d}{d\theta}(\cot^2\theta)=2\cot\theta(-\cosec^2\theta) =-\frac{2\cot\theta}{\sin^2\theta}. $$ (b) Divide by $\sin^2\theta$: $$ x\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\sec^2\theta-\frac{2\cot\theta}{\sin^2\theta} =\frac{d}{d\theta}\left(\tan\theta+\cot^2\theta\right). $$ Thus $$ \frac12x^2=\tan\theta+\cot^2\theta+C. $$ At $\theta=\pi/4,x=2$, $C=0$. Therefore $$ x^2=2(\tan\theta+\cot^2\theta). $$ At $\theta=\pi/6$, $$ \boxed{x=\sqrt{6+\frac2{\sqrt3}}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_32.pdf`, Q7(a–b), and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q10} ### Question 10 · 9709/31/M/J/23 Q7 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \cos 2x\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4\tan 2x}{\sin^2 3y}, $$ where $0\le x<\frac14\pi$. It is given that $y=0$ when $x=\frac16\pi$. Solve the differential equation to obtain the value of $x$ when $y=\frac16\pi$. Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places. **[8]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Separate and integrate: $$ \sin^2(3y)\,dy=\frac{4\sin2x}{\cos^2 2x}\,dx. $$ Hence $$ \frac y2-\frac{\sin6y}{12}=2\sec2x+C. $$ At $(x,y)=(\pi/6,0)$, $C=-4$. When $y=\pi/6$, $$ \frac\pi{12}=2\sec2x-4 \Longrightarrow \sec2x=2+\frac\pi{24}. $$ Thus $$ x=\frac12\cos^{-1}\left(\frac1{2+\pi/24}\right) \approx\boxed{0.568}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_31.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ### Further separable models ::: {.question-card #de-q11} ### Question 11 · 9709/32/M/J/23 Q8(a) The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4+9y^2}{e^{2x+1}}. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $x=1$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{4+9y^2}=e^{-(2x+1)}dx. $$ Integrating and using $y=0$ when $x=1$ gives $$ \frac16\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3y}{2}\right) =-\frac12e^{-(2x+1)}+\frac12e^{-3}. $$ Therefore $$ \boxed{y=\frac23\tan\left(3e^{-3}-3e^{-(2x+1)}\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_32.pdf`, Q8(a), and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q12} ### Question 12 · 9709/33/M/J/23 Q8 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y^2+4}{x(y+4)} $$ for $x>0$. It is given that $x=4$ when $y=2\sqrt3$. Solve the differential equation to obtain the value of $x$ when $y=2$. **[8]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Write the equation as $$ \frac{dx}{x}=\frac{y+4}{y^2+4}\,dy. $$ Then $$ \ln x=\frac12\ln(y^2+4)+2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac y2\right)+C. $$ At $x=4,y=2\sqrt3$, $C=-2\pi/3$. At $y=2$, $$ \ln x=\frac32\ln2-\frac\pi6, $$ so $$ \boxed{x=2\sqrt2\,e^{-\pi/6}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_33.pdf`, Q8, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q13} ### Question 13 · 9709/32/F/M/23 Q9 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=e^{3y}\sin^2 2x. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $x=0$. Solve the differential equation and find the value of $y$ when $x=\frac12$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ e^{-3y}dy=\sin^2 2x\,dx. $$ Using $\sin^2 2x=(1-\cos4x)/2$, $$ -\frac13e^{-3y}=\frac x2-\frac{\sin4x}{8}+C. $$ The initial condition gives $C=-1/3$, hence $$ e^{-3y}=1-\frac32x+\frac38\sin4x. $$ At $x=1/2$, $$ \boxed{y=-\frac13\ln\left(\frac14+\frac38\sin2\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_32.pdf`, Q9, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q14} ### Question 14 · 9709/31/O/N/23 Q7 The variables $x$ and $\phi$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{x}{\tan\phi}\frac{dx}{d\phi}=x^2+3. $$ It is given that $x=1$ when $\phi=0$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $x^2$ in terms of $\phi$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{x}{x^2+3}\,dx=\tan\phi\,d\phi. $$ Integrating, $$ \frac12\ln(x^2+3)=-\ln(\cos\phi)+C. $$ At $(x,\phi)=(1,0)$, $C=\ln2$. Therefore $$ \ln(x^2+3)=\ln(4\sec^2\phi), \qquad \boxed{x^2=4\sec^2\phi-3}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_31.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q15} ### Question 15 · 9709/32/O/N/23 Q11(a) The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ x^2\frac{dy}{dx}+y^2+y=0. $$ It is given that $x=1$ when $y=1$. (a) Solve the differential equation to obtain an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[8]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{y(y+1)}=-\frac{dx}{x^2}, \qquad \frac1{y(y+1)}=\frac1y-\frac1{y+1}. $$ Thus $$ \ln\left|\frac y{y+1}\right|=\frac1x+C. $$ At $(x,y)=(1,1)$, $C=-1-\ln2$. Hence $$ \frac y{y+1}=\frac12e^{1/x-1}. $$ Solving for $y$ gives $$ \boxed{y=\frac{e^{1/x-1}}{2-e^{1/x-1}}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_32.pdf`, Q11(a), and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q16} ### Question 16 · 9709/33/O/N/23 Q8 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ e^{4x}\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos^2 3y. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $x=2$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \sec^2(3y)\,dy=e^{-4x}\,dx. $$ After integration, $$ \frac13\tan3y=-\frac14e^{-4x}+C. $$ Using $y=0$ at $x=2$ gives $C=e^{-8}/4$. Thus $$ \boxed{y=\frac13\tan^{-1}\left(\frac34(e^{-8}-e^{-4x})\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_33.pdf`, Q8, and matching mark scheme.
::: ### Applied rate-of-change models ::: {.question-card #de-q17} ### Question 17 · 9709/32/F/M/24 Q11 The variables $y$ and $i$ satisfy the differential equation $$ (1+y)(1+\cos2i)\frac{dy}{di}=e^{3y}. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $i=\frac14\pi$. Solve the differential equation and find the exact value of $\tan i$ when $y=1$. **[9]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ (1+y)e^{-3y}dy=\frac{di}{1+\cos2i}=\frac12\sec^2i\,di. $$ Since $$ \int(1+y)e^{-3y}dy=-\frac{(3y+4)e^{-3y}}9, $$ the initial condition gives $$ -\frac{(3y+4)e^{-3y}}9=\frac12\tan i-\frac{17}{18}. $$ At $y=1$, $$ \boxed{\tan i=\frac{17-14e^{-3}}9}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2024/2024/A-Level-CAIE数学QP-202403-Mathematics-P32-A-Level题库大全小程序.pdf`, Q11, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q18} ### Question 18 · 9709/31/M/J/24 Q11 In a field there are 300 plants of a certain species, all of which can be infected by a particular disease. At time $t$ after the first plant is infected there are $x$ infected plants. The rate of change of $x$ is proportional to the product of the number of plants infected and the number of plants that are not yet infected. The variables $x$ and $t$ are treated as continuous, and it is given that $\frac{dx}{dt}=0.2$ and $x=1$ when $t=0$. (a) Show that $x$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ 1495\frac{dx}{dt}=x(300-x). $$ (b) Using partial fractions, solve the differential equation and obtain an expression for $t$ in terms of a single logarithm involving $x$. **[2+9]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer At $x=1$, the product is $1(299)$, so $0.2=k(299)$ and hence $k=1/1495$, proving (a). For (b), $$ \frac{1495\,dx}{x(300-x)}=dt, \qquad \frac1{x(300-x)}=\frac1{300}\left(\frac1x+\frac1{300-x}\right). $$ Using $x=1$ when $t=0$, $$ \frac{1495}{300}\ln\left(\frac{x}{300-x}\right) -\frac{1495}{300}\ln\left(\frac1{299}\right)=t. $$ Therefore $$ \boxed{t=\frac{1495}{300}\ln\left(\frac{299x}{300-x}\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2024/2024/A-Level-CAIE数学QP-202406-Mathematics-P31-A-Level题库大全小程序.pdf`, Q11, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q19} ### Question 19 · 9709/32/O/N/24 Q10 A balloon in the shape of a sphere has volume $V$ and radius $r$. Air is pumped into the balloon at a constant rate of $40\pi$ starting when time $t=0$ and $r=0$. At the same time, air begins to flow out of the balloon at a rate of $0.8\pi r$. The balloon remains a sphere at all times. (a) Show that $r$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{50-r}{5r^2}. $$ (b) Find the quotient and remainder when $5r^2$ is divided by $50-r$. (c) Solve the differential equation in part (a), obtaining an expression for $t$ in terms of $r$. **[3+3+6]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Since $V=\frac43\pi r^3$, $dV/dt=4\pi r^2\,dr/dt$. Equating net volume rate $40\pi-0.8\pi r$ gives (a). For (b), $$ \frac{5r^2}{50-r}=-5r-250+\frac{12500}{50-r}. $$ Therefore $$ \begin{aligned} t&=\int_0^r\frac{5s^2}{50-s}\,ds\\ &=\left[-\frac52s^2-250s+12500\ln\left(\frac{50}{50-s}\right)\right]_0^r. \end{aligned} $$ Hence $$ \boxed{t=-\frac52r^2-250r+12500\ln\left(\frac{50}{50-r}\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2024/2024/A-Level-CAIE数学QP-202410-Mathematics-P32-A-Level题库大全小程序.pdf`, Q10, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q20} ### Question 20 · 9709/33/O/N/22 Q10 A gardener is filling an ornamental pool with water, using a hose that delivers 30 litres of water per minute. Initially the pool is empty. At time $t$ minutes after filling begins the volume of water in the pool is $V$ litres. The pool has a small leak and loses water at a rate of 0.01V litres per minute. $$ \frac{dV}{dt}=a-bV. $$ (a) Write down the values of the constants $a$ and $b$. (b) Solve the differential equation and find the value of $t$ when $V=1000$. **[1+6]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer From the rates, $\boxed{a=30}$ and $\boxed{b=0.01}$. The equation is $$ \frac{dV}{dt}=30-0.01V. $$ Separate and use $V=0$ when $t=0$: $$ \frac{dV}{3000-V}=0.01\,dt \Longrightarrow -\ln(3000-V)=0.01t+C. $$ Hence $$ V=3000(1-e^{-0.01t}). $$ When $V=1000$, $$ e^{-0.01t}=\frac23 \Longrightarrow \boxed{t=100\ln\frac32\text{ minutes}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_33.pdf`, Q10, and matching mark scheme.
::: ## Exam checklist ::: {.study-card} 1. 分离变量时不要漏掉 $dy/dx$ 中的 $dx$ 或把 $e^{-x}$ 移错边。 2. 先积分，再使用 initial condition；积分常数通常决定最终 branch。 3. 三角积分要同时检查区间和 inverse-trigonometric branch。 4. 应用题先从 proportionality 写出常数，再用 given rate 求常数。 5. 最后把答案代回 differential equation 和 initial condition 检查。 :::

::: ::: {.question-card #de-q02} ### Question 2 · 9709/32/O/N/20 Q7 The variables $x$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ e^{3t}\frac{dx}{dt}=\cos^2 2x, $$ for $t\ge0$. It is given that $x=0$ when $t=0$. (a) Solve the differential equation and obtain an expression for $x$ in terms of $t$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \sec^2(2x)\,dx=e^{-3t}\,dt. $$ 积分得 $$ \frac12\tan(2x)=-\frac13e^{-3t}+C. $$ 代入 $x=0$ when $t=0$ 得 $C=1/3$，所以 $$ \tan(2x)=\frac23(1-e^{-3t}). $$ 由于 $x=0$ 时取 principal branch， $$ \boxed{x=\frac12\tan^{-1}\left(\frac23(1-e^{-3t})\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_32.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q03} ### Question 3 · 9709/32/F/M/21 Q4 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ (1-\cos x)\frac{dy}{dx}=y\sin x. $$ It is given that $y=4$ when $x=\pi$. (a) Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[6]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac1y\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\sin x}{1-\cos x} =\frac{d}{dx}\ln(1-\cos x). $$ 因此 $y=C(1-\cos x)$。由 $y=4$ when $x=\pi$： $$ 4=C(1-(-1))=2C\Longrightarrow C=2. $$ 故 $$ \boxed{y=2(1-\cos x)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_32.pdf`, Q4, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q04} ### Question 4 · 9709/31/M/J/21 Q10 The variables $x$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dx}{dt}=x^2(1+2x), $$ and $x=1$ when $t=0$. Using partial fractions, solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $t$ in terms of $x$. **[11]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dt}{dx}=\frac1{x^2(1+2x)} =-\frac2x+\frac1{x^2}+\frac4{1+2x}. $$ 积分并使用 $t=0$ when $x=1$： $$ t=-2\ln x-\frac1x+2\ln(1+2x)+1-2\ln3. $$ 整理为 $$ \boxed{t=2\ln\left(\frac{1+2x}{3x}\right)+1-\frac1x}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_31.pdf`, Q10, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q05} ### Question 5 · 9709/32/O/N/21 Q7 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ e^{2x}\frac{dy}{dx}=4xy^2, $$ and it is given that $y=1$ when $x=0$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ y^{-2}\,dy=4xe^{-2x}\,dx. $$ Since $$ \int4xe^{-2x}dx=-(2x+1)e^{-2x}, $$ we have $$ -\frac1y=-(2x+1)e^{-2x}+C. $$ At $(x,y)=(0,1)$, $C=0$. Hence $$ \boxed{y=\frac{e^{2x}}{2x+1}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_32.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q06} ### Question 6 · 9709/32/F/M/22 Q9 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ (x+1)(3x+1)\frac{dy}{dx}=y, $$ and it is given that $y=1$ when $x=1$. Solve the differential equation and find the exact value of $y$ when $x=3$, giving your answer in a simplified form. **[9]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{y}=\frac{dx}{(x+1)(3x+1)},qquad \frac1{(x+1)(3x+1)}=-\frac1{2(x+1)}+\frac3{2(3x+1)}. $$ Thus $$ \ln y=\frac12\ln\left(\frac{3x+1}{x+1}\right)+C. $$ Using $y=1$ at $x=1$ gives $C=\frac12\ln2$, so $$ y=\sqrt{\frac{2(3x+1)}{x+1}}. $$ At $x=3$, $$ \boxed{y=\sqrt5}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_32.pdf`, Q9, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q07} ### Question 7 · 9709/31/M/J/22 Q4 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{xy}{1+x^2}, $$ and $y=2$ when $x=0$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining a simplified expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{y}=\frac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx \Longrightarrow \ln y=\frac12\ln(1+x^2)+C. $$ At $x=0,y=2$, $C=\ln2$. Hence $$ \boxed{y=2\sqrt{1+x^2}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_31.pdf`, Q4, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q08} ### Question 8 · 9709/32/M/J/22 Q6 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=xe^{y-x}, $$ and $y=0$ when $x=0$. (a) Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ e^{-y}\,dy=xe^{-x}\,dx. $$ Integrating, $$ -e^{-y}=-(x+1)e^{-x}+C. $$ The initial condition gives $C=0$, so $$ e^{-y}=(x+1)e^{-x} \Longrightarrow \boxed{y=x-\ln(x+1)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_32.pdf`, Q6, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q09} ### Question 9 · 9709/32/O/N/22 Q7(a–b) The variables $x$ and $\theta$ satisfy the differential equation $$ x\sin^2\theta\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\tan^2\theta-2\cot\theta, $$ for $0<\theta<\frac12\pi$ and $x>0$. It is given that $x=2$ when $\theta=\frac14\pi$. (a) Show that $$ \frac{d}{d\theta}(\cot^2\theta)=-\frac{2\cot\theta}{\sin^2\theta}. $$ (You may assume without proof that the derivative of $\cot\theta$ with respect to $\theta$ is $-\cosec^2\theta$.) (b) Solve the differential equation and find the value of $x$ when $\theta=\frac16\pi$. **[1+7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer (a) $$ \frac{d}{d\theta}(\cot^2\theta)=2\cot\theta(-\cosec^2\theta) =-\frac{2\cot\theta}{\sin^2\theta}. $$ (b) Divide by $\sin^2\theta$: $$ x\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\sec^2\theta-\frac{2\cot\theta}{\sin^2\theta} =\frac{d}{d\theta}\left(\tan\theta+\cot^2\theta\right). $$ Thus $$ \frac12x^2=\tan\theta+\cot^2\theta+C. $$ At $\theta=\pi/4,x=2$, $C=0$. Therefore $$ x^2=2(\tan\theta+\cot^2\theta). $$ At $\theta=\pi/6$, $$ \boxed{x=\sqrt{6+\frac2{\sqrt3}}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_32.pdf`, Q7(a–b), and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q10} ### Question 10 · 9709/31/M/J/23 Q7 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \cos 2x\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4\tan 2x}{\sin^2 3y}, $$ where $0\le x<\frac14\pi$. It is given that $y=0$ when $x=\frac16\pi$. Solve the differential equation to obtain the value of $x$ when $y=\frac16\pi$. Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places. **[8]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Separate and integrate: $$ \sin^2(3y)\,dy=\frac{4\sin2x}{\cos^2 2x}\,dx. $$ Hence $$ \frac y2-\frac{\sin6y}{12}=2\sec2x+C. $$ At $(x,y)=(\pi/6,0)$, $C=-4$. When $y=\pi/6$, $$ \frac\pi{12}=2\sec2x-4 \Longrightarrow \sec2x=2+\frac\pi{24}. $$ Thus $$ x=\frac12\cos^{-1}\left(\frac1{2+\pi/24}\right) \approx\boxed{0.568}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_31.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ### Further separable models ::: {.question-card #de-q11} ### Question 11 · 9709/32/M/J/23 Q8(a) The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4+9y^2}{e^{2x+1}}. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $x=1$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{4+9y^2}=e^{-(2x+1)}dx. $$ Integrating and using $y=0$ when $x=1$ gives $$ \frac16\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3y}{2}\right) =-\frac12e^{-(2x+1)}+\frac12e^{-3}. $$ Therefore $$ \boxed{y=\frac23\tan\left(3e^{-3}-3e^{-(2x+1)}\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_32.pdf`, Q8(a), and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q12} ### Question 12 · 9709/33/M/J/23 Q8 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y^2+4}{x(y+4)} $$ for $x>0$. It is given that $x=4$ when $y=2\sqrt3$. Solve the differential equation to obtain the value of $x$ when $y=2$. **[8]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Write the equation as $$ \frac{dx}{x}=\frac{y+4}{y^2+4}\,dy. $$ Then $$ \ln x=\frac12\ln(y^2+4)+2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac y2\right)+C. $$ At $x=4,y=2\sqrt3$, $C=-2\pi/3$. At $y=2$, $$ \ln x=\frac32\ln2-\frac\pi6, $$ so $$ \boxed{x=2\sqrt2\,e^{-\pi/6}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_33.pdf`, Q8, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q13} ### Question 13 · 9709/32/F/M/23 Q9 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dy}{dx}=e^{3y}\sin^2 2x. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $x=0$. Solve the differential equation and find the value of $y$ when $x=\frac12$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ e^{-3y}dy=\sin^2 2x\,dx. $$ Using $\sin^2 2x=(1-\cos4x)/2$, $$ -\frac13e^{-3y}=\frac x2-\frac{\sin4x}{8}+C. $$ The initial condition gives $C=-1/3$, hence $$ e^{-3y}=1-\frac32x+\frac38\sin4x. $$ At $x=1/2$, $$ \boxed{y=-\frac13\ln\left(\frac14+\frac38\sin2\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_32.pdf`, Q9, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q14} ### Question 14 · 9709/31/O/N/23 Q7 The variables $x$ and $\phi$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{x}{\tan\phi}\frac{dx}{d\phi}=x^2+3. $$ It is given that $x=1$ when $\phi=0$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $x^2$ in terms of $\phi$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{x}{x^2+3}\,dx=\tan\phi\,d\phi. $$ Integrating, $$ \frac12\ln(x^2+3)=-\ln(\cos\phi)+C. $$ At $(x,\phi)=(1,0)$, $C=\ln2$. Therefore $$ \ln(x^2+3)=\ln(4\sec^2\phi), \qquad \boxed{x^2=4\sec^2\phi-3}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_31.pdf`, Q7, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q15} ### Question 15 · 9709/32/O/N/23 Q11(a) The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ x^2\frac{dy}{dx}+y^2+y=0. $$ It is given that $x=1$ when $y=1$. (a) Solve the differential equation to obtain an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[8]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \frac{dy}{y(y+1)}=-\frac{dx}{x^2}, \qquad \frac1{y(y+1)}=\frac1y-\frac1{y+1}. $$ Thus $$ \ln\left|\frac y{y+1}\right|=\frac1x+C. $$ At $(x,y)=(1,1)$, $C=-1-\ln2$. Hence $$ \frac y{y+1}=\frac12e^{1/x-1}. $$ Solving for $y$ gives $$ \boxed{y=\frac{e^{1/x-1}}{2-e^{1/x-1}}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_32.pdf`, Q11(a), and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q16} ### Question 16 · 9709/33/O/N/23 Q8 The variables $x$ and $y$ satisfy the differential equation $$ e^{4x}\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos^2 3y. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $x=2$. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for $y$ in terms of $x$. **[7]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ \sec^2(3y)\,dy=e^{-4x}\,dx. $$ After integration, $$ \frac13\tan3y=-\frac14e^{-4x}+C. $$ Using $y=0$ at $x=2$ gives $C=e^{-8}/4$. Thus $$ \boxed{y=\frac13\tan^{-1}\left(\frac34(e^{-8}-e^{-4x})\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_33.pdf`, Q8, and matching mark scheme.
::: ### Applied rate-of-change models ::: {.question-card #de-q17} ### Question 17 · 9709/32/F/M/24 Q11 The variables $y$ and $i$ satisfy the differential equation $$ (1+y)(1+\cos2i)\frac{dy}{di}=e^{3y}. $$ It is given that $y=0$ when $i=\frac14\pi$. Solve the differential equation and find the exact value of $\tan i$ when $y=1$. **[9]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer $$ (1+y)e^{-3y}dy=\frac{di}{1+\cos2i}=\frac12\sec^2i\,di. $$ Since $$ \int(1+y)e^{-3y}dy=-\frac{(3y+4)e^{-3y}}9, $$ the initial condition gives $$ -\frac{(3y+4)e^{-3y}}9=\frac12\tan i-\frac{17}{18}. $$ At $y=1$, $$ \boxed{\tan i=\frac{17-14e^{-3}}9}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2024/2024/A-Level-CAIE数学QP-202403-Mathematics-P32-A-Level题库大全小程序.pdf`, Q11, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q18} ### Question 18 · 9709/31/M/J/24 Q11 In a field there are 300 plants of a certain species, all of which can be infected by a particular disease. At time $t$ after the first plant is infected there are $x$ infected plants. The rate of change of $x$ is proportional to the product of the number of plants infected and the number of plants that are not yet infected. The variables $x$ and $t$ are treated as continuous, and it is given that $\frac{dx}{dt}=0.2$ and $x=1$ when $t=0$. (a) Show that $x$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ 1495\frac{dx}{dt}=x(300-x). $$ (b) Using partial fractions, solve the differential equation and obtain an expression for $t$ in terms of a single logarithm involving $x$. **[2+9]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer At $x=1$, the product is $1(299)$, so $0.2=k(299)$ and hence $k=1/1495$, proving (a). For (b), $$ \frac{1495\,dx}{x(300-x)}=dt, \qquad \frac1{x(300-x)}=\frac1{300}\left(\frac1x+\frac1{300-x}\right). $$ Using $x=1$ when $t=0$, $$ \frac{1495}{300}\ln\left(\frac{x}{300-x}\right) -\frac{1495}{300}\ln\left(\frac1{299}\right)=t. $$ Therefore $$ \boxed{t=\frac{1495}{300}\ln\left(\frac{299x}{300-x}\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2024/2024/A-Level-CAIE数学QP-202406-Mathematics-P31-A-Level题库大全小程序.pdf`, Q11, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q19} ### Question 19 · 9709/32/O/N/24 Q10 A balloon in the shape of a sphere has volume $V$ and radius $r$. Air is pumped into the balloon at a constant rate of $40\pi$ starting when time $t=0$ and $r=0$. At the same time, air begins to flow out of the balloon at a rate of $0.8\pi r$. The balloon remains a sphere at all times. (a) Show that $r$ and $t$ satisfy the differential equation $$ \frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{50-r}{5r^2}. $$ (b) Find the quotient and remainder when $5r^2$ is divided by $50-r$. (c) Solve the differential equation in part (a), obtaining an expression for $t$ in terms of $r$. **[3+3+6]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer Since $V=\frac43\pi r^3$, $dV/dt=4\pi r^2\,dr/dt$. Equating net volume rate $40\pi-0.8\pi r$ gives (a). For (b), $$ \frac{5r^2}{50-r}=-5r-250+\frac{12500}{50-r}. $$ Therefore $$ \begin{aligned} t&=\int_0^r\frac{5s^2}{50-s}\,ds\\ &=\left[-\frac52s^2-250s+12500\ln\left(\frac{50}{50-s}\right)\right]_0^r. \end{aligned} $$ Hence $$ \boxed{t=-\frac52r^2-250r+12500\ln\left(\frac{50}{50-r}\right)}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2024/2024/A-Level-CAIE数学QP-202410-Mathematics-P32-A-Level题库大全小程序.pdf`, Q10, and matching mark scheme.
::: ::: {.question-card #de-q20} ### Question 20 · 9709/33/O/N/22 Q10 A gardener is filling an ornamental pool with water, using a hose that delivers 30 litres of water per minute. Initially the pool is empty. At time $t$ minutes after filling begins the volume of water in the pool is $V$ litres. The pool has a small leak and loses water at a rate of 0.01V litres per minute. $$ \frac{dV}{dt}=a-bV. $$ (a) Write down the values of the constants $a$ and $b$. (b) Solve the differential equation and find the value of $t$ when $V=1000$. **[1+6]**
Show detailed mark scheme answer From the rates, $\boxed{a=30}$ and $\boxed{b=0.01}$. The equation is $$ \frac{dV}{dt}=30-0.01V. $$ Separate and use $V=0$ when $t=0$: $$ \frac{dV}{3000-V}=0.01\,dt \Longrightarrow -\ln(3000-V)=0.01t+C. $$ Hence $$ V=3000(1-e^{-0.01t}). $$ When $V=1000$, $$ e^{-0.01t}=\frac23 \Longrightarrow \boxed{t=100\ln\frac32\text{ minutes}}. $$
Source: `PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_33.pdf`, Q10, and matching mark scheme.
::: ## Exam checklist ::: {.study-card} 1. 分离变量时不要漏掉 $dy/dx$ 中的 $dx$ 或把 $e^{-x}$ 移错边。 2. 先积分，再使用 initial condition；积分常数通常决定最终 branch。 3. 三角积分要同时检查区间和 inverse-trigonometric branch。 4. 应用题先从 proportionality 写出常数，再用 given rate 求常数。 5. 最后把答案代回 differential equation 和 initial condition 检查。 :::
